text.p: Argus Research analyst Wendy Abramowitz said she is reducing her 1997 earnings estimate for Imation Corp to $1.27 per share from $1.55 per share.

She said she took the action based on the company's announcement late Tuesday and conference call early Wednesday regarding its expectation that net income and earnings per share for the second quarter ending June 30 will fall below analysts' estimates.
Shares in Imation were off 1-3/16 to 24-1/4.
Prior to the announcement, the First Call consensus of four analysts' Imation earnings estimates was $0.33 per share for the second quarter and $1.48 per share for the year.
The company said Tuesday that operating margins for the second quarter will likely be in the low single digits.
It cited "weaker than expected demand for several lower-capacity data storage products -- including the low end Travan minicartridges -- resulting in lower gross margins than previously planned."

On Wednesday after the conference call, Imation spokesman Brent Bauer said "It's premature to suggest that this is a trend ... We knew this year was going to be a turbulent year as we started to work our plan."

The company is making a transition to higher-capacity data storage products and expects to introduce products in 1998 based on near field recording technology and a new half-inch tape cartridge format.
Imation is scheduled to announce second quarter earnings on July 30.
Other analysts contacted Wednesday morning said they were considering revisions to their earnings estimates, as well.
